title: Rule Fourteen
logline: A rumor that Pam is moving to Stamford spreads through the office like a game of telephone, and Michael's farewell speech for her turns into a sincere speech about the office.
outline: A: Kelly's rumor that Pam is moving to Stamford reaches Roy; Michael relays Jim's call badly; Pam tells Roy she is staying in Scranton and writes her answer on a napkin. B: Toby enforces Rule Fourteen (no banjo hold music) and Michael makes it personal; Michael's farewell speech for Pam becomes a sincere speech about the office. C: Dwight and Andy time their Thursday turns at the break room table while Stanley sits at 187. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, A, B, A, C, tag.
theme: Who do you choose when you finally have to choose? Showing up for people versus being chosen by them.
storySoFar: Jim is in Stamford dating Shannon and working with Karen; his unanswered card sits in Pam's drawer beside the Stamford paints. Pam has told Roy she is not happy; June 14 is still on. Pam is taking Tuesday watercolor classes, which Michael knows about and says he will keep quiet about, or maybe not. Michael has stopped chasing favorites: he asked Toby how he is and waited for the answer, and he gave the office a real speech. Corporate called his letters unnecessary. Dwight and Andy share the Pruitt account and will drive to Dale's office Thursday, speaking in turns. Stanley is stuck at 187 days; Michael's joke dies, and Kevin closes with "Nobody say nothing." Jan's candles and Kelly's party fights are behind them. Andy's banjo hold music continues to annoy Toby.

stateChanges.progress: Rumor says Pam is moving to Stamford; Pam tells Roy she is staying in Scranton but not that she is staying with him. She writes her answer to Jim on a napkin and has not sent it. Jim knows Michael relayed 'not a no'.

stateChanges.arc: Michael Wants to Be the Favorite
stateChanges.progress: Michael gives a sincere speech to the office about showing up, and Toby's Rule Fourteen becomes a fight he almost picks and then sits out.

stateChanges.arc: Dwight vs Andy for Number Two
stateChanges.progress: Thursday turns agreed at the break room table: Dwight four minutes, Andy four minutes, nobody goes over.
Still at 187. Stanley says Michael's speech was 'dull, but you meant it' and nods.

stateChanges.status: wedding on, Pam not happy and no longer hiding it; she said she is staying in Scranton, not with him

stateChanges.text: Kelly's rumor (Pam moving to Stamford with Jim) is still circulating; Roy heard it first and is suspicious.
Pam's napkin answer to Jim is folded in her drawer with the Stamford paints.
Telephone game: each person repeats a rumor a little bigger; Kevin says 'Pam go Stamford' and Oscar corrects him.

Stanley at 187; Michael's 'That's what she said' dies on silence; Kevin closes with 'Nobody say nothing.'

scenes.recap: Michael tries the countdown joke on Stanley at 187 and it dies on silence; Kevin closes it out.

beats.text: A hundred and eighty-seven days, Stanley. That's a lot of days. That's what she said.
Did I stutter?

lines: Michael says it every day. Same joke. Every day I am exactly where I was, which is at a desk.

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Kelly tells Phyllis Pam is moving to Stamford, and the rumor gets bigger as it passes to Kevin and Oscar.

beats.text: Pam's moving to Stamford. Karen told me Jim already got her a desk.
Pam didn't say that.
Pam doesn't say things, Phyllis. That's her whole thing.

lines: I didn't start it. I just said it faster than anybody else in the building.

beats.text: Pam go Stamford.
Kevin, Karen said there is a desk. She did not say Pam is going.
Desk. Stamford. Same word.
I'm telling Roy.
Kelly, don't.

scenes.recap: Toby posts Rule Fourteen after Andy's banjo hold music interrupts the bullpen, and Michael makes the rule about Toby.

beats.caption: holds up bear-paw phone as banjo hold music twangs

beats.text: Andy, Rule Fourteen. No instruments on hold during business hours.
It's not an instrument, Toby. It's a feeling on hold.
Actually, it's a banjo on hold.
Toby, Rule Fourteen is about you. You don't want anybody having fun, because nobody invited you to have fun.

lines: I'm trying to enforce a policy. He makes it about my childhood. He doesn't know anything about my childhood.

beats.text: I'm canceling Rule Fourteen. Effective now. I'm the regional manager and I'm canceling it with my mouth.
You can't cancel a rule by saying it.
Watch me.

beats.caption: Toby looks at the banjo ringtone.

scenes.recap: Dwight times Andy's Thursday turns with a stopwatch while Stanley stares at the clock, stuck at 187.

beats.caption: sets a stopwatch on the table between two Dixie cups

beats.text: Question: who speaks first at Dale's office Thursday?
Me. I have the Cornell voice. Dale responds to the Cornell voice.
False. Dale responds to beets. And I have the Pruitt history.
Okay. You go first. Four minutes. Then I do the close.
Four minutes, me. Four minutes, you. Nobody goes over. I will be timing you.
Dwight, you're timing my laugh.
Are you two going to talk about Dale's, or who is older? I'm at a hundred and eighty-seven.
Partners.
Partners. Thursday. Do not go over, Dwight.

scenes.recap: Michael promises to keep the rumor quiet, then answers Jim's call and relays Pam's words as 'not a no.'

beats.text: Pam, I'm not going to say anything. I'm a vault. A vault with a Hallmark card.
Michael, Kelly told the whole building I'm moving to Stamford.
Kelly didn't tell me. Kelly told the air conditioning.

beats.caption: grabs Pam's ringing line and answers it

beats.text: Dunder Mifflin, Scranton, Michael Scott, Regional Manager. Jim? Hi, buddy.
Michael. Give me the phone.
She's right here. She's not moving to Stamford. She said that. I'm the one who's saying it, though.
She didn't say she's staying either. But she said it's not a no.
I said not here.
You said not here. Which is basically what she said.

lines: She said not here. Michael said it's not a no. I'm in Stamford, and I just got a yes from a man holding a receiver like a trophy.

scenes.recap: Michael gives a sincere speech about the office, which he had written for Pam's farewell, and Kelly calls it disgusting.

beats.text: I wrote a speech for Pam's going-away. It's called 'Your Desk Is Still Here.' Pam, I'm sorry.
I'm not leaving, Michael.
Right. Okay. Then this is for the office. Which is sort of the same thing.

lines: I used to think the job was being the favorite. Then I read the letters, and they were scared. I don't want scared. I want people to show up.

beats.text: You're here. Even when you hate it. Even Toby, who's sitting down right now. Thank you for sitting.
Thank you.
Michael, that's disgusting.
Keep going.
That's the speech. That's all I had.
Did I stutter? Can we go?

scenes.recap: Roy corners Pam at the smoking spot about Kelly's rumor, and Pam says she is staying in Scranton, not with him.

beats.text: Kelly says you're moving to Stamford.
Kelly says a lot of things.
Are you?
No.
Good. So you're staying with me.
I'm staying in Scranton.
That's not what I asked.

beats.caption: Pam looks at the parking lot.

beats.text: I know.

lines: He asked me a yes or no. I gave him a Scranton. I know that's a bad answer. It was the only true one I had.

scenes.recap: Michael tries to cancel Rule Fourteen by speech, asks Toby if he likes banjos, and Oscar gives the banjo gag a correction.

beats.text: Rule Fourteen is still in effect.
Toby, it's not a rule, it's a Cornell heartbeat.
Toby, I'm going to ask you a real question. Do you like banjos?
No.
Okay. Okay. Andy, play Toby something he hates.

beats.caption: launches into an a cappella Cornell fight song at full volume

beats.text: Actually, that's a banjo on hold, and now it's a choir.
I'm going to the fire exit.
Toby, don't go. I'm being present. Look at me being present.

beats.caption: sits down at his desk and does not leave

scenes.recap: Pam writes her answer to Jim on a napkin and folds it into her drawer, telling Phyllis she will say it in person.

beats.caption: writes three careful lines on a folded napkin

beats.text: Is it a yes?
It's a napkin.
Pam, a napkin is going to be a problem.
I'm going to tell him in person. Not on Michael's phone.

lines: I wrote it on a napkin because a napkin doesn't have a binder. It has a corner. I can fold it.

beats.caption: slides the folded napkin into her desk drawer beside the Stamford paints

scenes.recap: Michael tries the countdown joke again, and Stanley says Michael's speech was dull but he meant it.

beats.text: Stanley, it's a hundred and eighty-seven. Does that mean it's stuck, or it's coming?
It's a hundred and eighty-seven.
That's what she said.
Your speech was dull. But you meant it.
Thank you, Stanley.

scenes.recap: After hours, Kevin repeats the rumor wrong one last time, and Michael's joke dies before Kevin closes the scene.

beats.text: Pam go Stamford. Stanley go home.
I'm not going anywhere, Kevin.
A hundred and eighty-seven. Think of how many days that's been. That's what she said.
Nobody say nothing.
